summary: Preserve computed class field names, which are evaluated once during class definition while the field initializer is evaluated per instance.

target.notes: Use the JavaScript-compatible class/object model so the computed key is captured at class evaluation and later used to define an own field on each instance.

caveats: C# member names are compile-time identifiers and cannot directly represent arbitrary JavaScript property keys or Symbols.

tests.name: computed key evaluated once
tests.input: let n=0; const key=()=>('x'+(++n)); class C { [key()] = 1; } new C(); new C(); console.log(n);

tests.name: edge: initializer remains per instance
tests.input: let n=0; class C { ['x'] = ++n; } console.log(new C().x, new C().x);
